content: 1. Abemaciclib and Strong CYP3A4 Inhibitors: Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors increase plasma levels of abemaciclib and its metabolites by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. This necessitates a reduction in the abemaciclib dose. If the strong CYP3A4 inhibitor is discontinued, the abemaciclib dose should be increased to the level used prior to the initiation of the inhibitor. Close monitoring is required during therapy adjustments. 2. Tipranavir and Acarbose: Tipranavir decreases the effects of acarbose through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Caution is advised, and patients should be monitored for changes in glycemic control. Protease inhibitors, including tipranavir, have been associated with new-onset or worsening diabetes mellitus and hyperglycemia. 3. Tipranavir and Albiglutide: Tipranavir reduces the effects of albiglutide, likely due to insulin resistance induced by protease inhibitors. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 4. Tipranavir and Alfentanil: Tipranavir increases alfentanil levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are necessary to avoid potential toxicity. 5. Tipranavir and Amlodipine: Tipranavir increases amlodipine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, which may lead to increased toxicity. Caution and monitoring are advised. 6. Tipranavir and Amobarbital: Amobarbital decreases tipranavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 7. Tipranavir and Antithrombin Alfa/Antithrombin III: Tipranavir enhances the effects of antithrombin alfa and antithrombin III through pharmacodynamic synergy. This, combined with tipranavir’s mild antiplatelet activity, may increase bleeding risk. Caution and monitoring are advised. 8. Tipranavir and Apalutamide: Tipranavir increases apalutamide levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. While initial dose modification may not be required, dose adjustments may be necessary based on tolerability. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 9. Tipranavir and Apixaban: Tipranavir increases apixaban levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially increasing bleeding risk. Caution and monitoring are advised. 10. Tipranavir and Aprepitant: Aprepitant increases tipranavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 11. Tipranavir and Argatroban: Tipranavir enhances the effects of argatroban through pharmacodynamic synergy, increasing bleeding risk. Caution and monitoring are advised. 12. Tipranavir and Armodafinil: Armodafinil decreases tipranavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 13. Tipranavir and Artemether/Lumefantrine: Tipranavir decreases the levels of artemether/lumefantrine and vice versa, due to CYP3A4 metabolism interactions. Caution and monitoring are advised. 14. Tipranavir and Atazanavir: Atazanavir increases tipranavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 15. Tipranavir and Atogepant: Tipranavir increases atogepant levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The recommended atogepant dose is 10 mg once daily when coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Therapy should be modified and closely monitored. 16. Tipranavir and Atomoxetine: Tipranavir increases atomoxetine levels by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 17. Tipranavir and Bemiparin: Tipranavir enhances the effects of bemiparin through pharmacodynamic synergy, increasing bleeding risk. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 18. Tipranavir and Benzhydrocodone/Acetaminophen: Tipranavir increases the levels of benzhydrocodone (a prodrug of hydrocodone) by inhibiting CYP3A4 and CYP2D6 metabolism. This can lead to potentially fatal respiratory depression. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 19. Tipranavir and Berotralstat: Tipranavir decreases berotralstat levels by affecting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 20. Tipranavir and Bexarotene: Tipranavir increases bexarotene levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially increasing toxicity. Therapy should be modified, and alternatives should be considered if available. 21. Tipranavir and Bivalirudin: Tipranavir enhances the effects of bivalirudin through pharmacodynamic synergy, increasing bleeding risk. Caution and monitoring are advised. 22. Tipranavir and Bortezomib: Tipranavir increases bortezomib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 23. Tipranavir and Bosentan: Bosentan decreases tipranavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 24. Tipranavir and Brentuximab Vedotin: Tipranavir increases brentuximab vedotin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Patients should be monitored for adverse reactions. 25. Tipranavir and Brexpiprazole: Tipranavir increases brexpiprazole levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The brexpiprazole dose should be halved when coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. If a CYP2D6 inhibitor is also used, the dose should be reduced to one-quarter. 26. Tipranavir and Bromocriptine: Tipranavir increases bromocriptine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 27. Tipranavir and Budesonide: Budesonide decreases tipranavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 28. Tipranavir and Buprenorphine: Tipranavir increases buprenorphine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and patients should be monitored for signs of overmedication or withdrawal. 29. Tipranavir and Butabarbital/Butalbital: Both drugs decrease tipranavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 30. Tipranavir and Cabazitaxel: Tipranavir increases cabazitaxel levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially increasing toxicity. Coadministration should be avoided. 31. Tipranavir and Calcifediol: Tipranavir affects vitamin D metabolism by inhibiting CYP3A4, CYP24A1, and CYP27B1 enzymes. This may alter serum calcifediol levels and reduce its conversion to calcitriol. Dose adjustments and close monitoring of vitamin D, PTH, and calcium levels are required. 32. Tipranavir and Cannabidiol: Tipranavir increases cannabidiol levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and the cannabidiol dose may need to be reduced. 33. Tipranavir and Capmatinib: Tipranavir increases capmatinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 34. Tipranavir and Carbamazepine: Tipranavir increases carbamazepine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Plasma levels should be monitored. 35. Tipranavir and Cariprazine: Tipranavir increases cariprazine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Dose reduction is required when coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 36. Tipranavir and Carvedilol: Tipranavir increases carvedilol levels by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 37. Tipranavir and Chlordiazepoxide: Tipranavir increases chlordiazepoxide levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Alternatives should be considered, and benzodiazepine doses may need to be lowered. 38. Tipranavir and Cholic Acid: Tipranavir increases cholic acid toxicity by reducing its elimination. Coadministration with bile salt efflux pump inhibitors should be avoided. If necessary, monitor liver function closely. 39. Tipranavir and Cilostazol: Tipranavir increases cilostazol levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 40. Tipranavir and Citalopram: Tipranavir increases citalopram levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 41. Tipranavir and Clomipramine: Tipranavir increases clomipramine levels by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 42. Tipranavir and Clonazepam: Tipranavir increases clonazepam levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Alternatives should be considered, and benzodiazepine doses may need to be lowered. 43. Tipranavir and Clorazepate: Tipranavir increases clorazepate levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Alternatives should be considered, and benzodiazepine doses may need to be lowered. 44. Tipranavir and Colchicine: Tipranavir increases colchicine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Dose reduction is recommended, and colchicine is contraindicated in patients with renal or hepatic impairment. 45. Tipranavir and Conivaptan: Conivaptan increases tipranavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 46. Tipranavir and Cortisone: Cortisone decreases tipranavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 47. Tipranavir and Crizotinib: Tipranavir increases crizotinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors should be avoided. 48. Tipranavir and Crofelemer: Crofelemer increases tipranavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism in the gut. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 49. Tipranavir and Cyclophosphamide: Tipranavir increases cyclophosphamide levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 50. Tipranavir and Cyclosporine: Cyclosporine levels may increase or decrease due to contradictory effects of tipranavir on CYP3A4 and P-glycoprotein. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 51. Tipranavir and Dabrafenib: Dabrafenib decreases tipranavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 52. Tipranavir and Dalteparin: Tipranavir enhances the effects of dalteparin through pharmacodynamic synergy, increasing bleeding risk. Caution and monitoring are advised. 53. Tipranavir and Darifenacin: Tipranavir increases darifenacin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 54. Tipranavir and Darolutamide: Tipranavir increases darolutamide levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 and P-glycoprotein. Close monitoring and dose adjustments are required. 55. Tipranavir and Darunavir: Darunavir increases tipranavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 56. Tipranavir and Dasatinib: Dasatinib increases tipranavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 57. Tipranavir and Deferasirox: Deferasirox decreases tipranavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 58. Tipranavir and Deflazacort: Tipranavir increases deflazacort levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The deflazacort dose should be reduced to one-third when coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 59. Tipranavir and Desipramine: Tipranavir increases desipramine levels by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 60. Tipranavir and Deutetrabenazine: Tipranavir increases deutetrabenazine levels by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. The deutetrabenazine dose should not exceed 18 mg per dose and 36 mg per day when coadministered with strong CYP2D6 inhibitors. ...
